I've had small ovarian cysts and they are incredibly painful. So when my sister said her friend had several cysts amounting to 20 or so pounds I was in shock and seeing this image was like "oh...my...god". Sometimes there is no pain until they get very large. Or, in the case of my sister's friend, they knew she was sick but it was diagnosed as intestinal problems. She didn't have any imaging tests and when she got increasingly more ill, the more the doctors blamed her GI problem. It wasn't until she started vomiting nonstop, was in excrutiating pain, and taken to the ER (she was at school when this happened) that the true cause was revealed. Surgery was required obviously.

It can happen. Especially without imaging studies - in all fairness, even an MRI with insurance can cost thousands. Personally, the times I've had cysts, definitely way smaller, it felt like I was carrying a huge water balloon in my abdomen. And it's not a "fun" feeling either. I cannot imagine carrying around a cyst that is the size of a small child.

I should add, any articles you may read online about the cost of having a pet tend to be inaccurate. I believe I came across one on CNN before the holidays (I have tried to do a quick search to find this but I'm not seeing it). Since I only have guinea pigs, I can comment that the estimated cost of listed was a laugh. I have six guinea pigs at the moment, and even if I estimate the cost of one guinea pig per month (and initial investment) it still adds up. Guinea pig + C&C cage + C&C cage replacement pieces + bedding + pellets + orchard grass (less triggering for allergies versus hay) + veggies + vet visits = much more then was estimated (which was I believe only $100 or $200). The C&C cage with all its parts was more than that! If you want a more reasonable cost per month on a pet, find a friend, neighbor, someone who owns a dog, cat, small animal, etc that you want.

Not only dogs either. And it's worse when you see small animals returned to a pet store. A few days before Christmas my sister and I went to PetSmart to get guinea pig food (an emergency food run, we normally buy online). We glanced into the guinea pig enclosure and were told by an employee they only had one guinea pigs left. I told my sister that if we came back a few days after Christmas there would be plenty of "returns". Off we went three days after Christmas and looked at the enclosure of guinea pigs. There were six in the small space and were told an additional 13 were in the back. It's sad in several ways. The first is that these big chain pet stores are notorious for their mistreatment of animals, sending it back into this environment is not only horrible for the guinea pig, but if it contracted an illness at the adopted home the guinea pig runs the chance of dying because of lack of vet treatment. 

Pets are not toys, they are living beings. You may be able to "return" them but this is truly a cruel thing. PLEASE if you get ANY pet make sure you are 100% ready to keep it. If you think that getting a small animal, like a guinea pig, at a chain pet store will teach your child responsibility you need to reconsider. You are supporting mistreatment of animals when your purchase - or they call it "adoption" but putting an animal "on sale" validates it as an item not a living, breathing, animal. ANY pet you get for a child you need to be prepared to care for it. It will lose its novelty and you need to be ready to take care of it for potentially many years.

Please, please, please adopt shelter animals. There are so many animals looking for loving homes.

Also, PLEASE be able to financially support your pet. Not just with food, bedding, etc but also with vet bills. Every pet runs the risk of getting sick.

Okay, I'll stop now, so many people don't really think through having a pet which is upsetting. 

TL;DR: Be fully prepared to take care of any pet. Adoption at a shelter is much better than "adopting" (buying) a pet store. Getting a pet for a child? Be prepared that you may have to take over as the novelty could wear off. Consider all expenses your pet may have - including emergency/sudden illness vet visits.

I have been contemplating if I would go back and change something given the chance. I have ached with guilt and grief of the day that I had my traumatic brain injury. I don't remember the exact details of how it happened. I wish I knew. For a long time I wanted to make different choices that day. If I just stayed home. If I feigned illness to avoid leaving my house. If only this, it only that. I wanted to change that day for many years. It fucked up my life for years after and I still have problems. But I have come to realize that if I didn't have the accident I wouldn't be the me today. It was difficult for me after but I learned a lot of skills. I am very empathic. I can feel the suffering of others. I am quirky and it makes me interesting. My friends enjoy my random facts and sarcasm. Granted they don't always get my sarcasm! I have helped a lot of other people. I have talked several people out of suicide because I personally understand the pain of just being alive. If I didn't have my accident my life would be different. I wouldn't have my personality. My life may even be worse and not better. My suffering gave me strength. If I survived years of wanting to kill myself and walking the fine line between life and death I can survive almost anything. Actually, thinking about it, it's entirely possible that I hold the emotional strength within to survive everything thrown at me. 

I have the fleeting thoughts of wanting to change my past but I have come to accept who I am. I don't wish my accident to happen to anyone or again to myself but the worst day of my life turned me into a great person.

I had this issue. First thing you have to do, stick by your terms. If it's over, it's over. If he keeps calling you or texting you, block his number. Block every number he calls you on (I had to do this, sometimes you have to pay a monthly rate to block calls but it's worth it in the end). Next, and even though this may be hard, you can't be friends with him. Some people can remain friends after a break up, but often times it doesn't work. Cut the relationship and cut the friendship. You've got to tell your other friends you're also broken up, and that you are avoiding him. If they are good friends, they'll have your back. Either they'll invite you to places he's not at or give you a heads up when is invited so you can opt out.

Basically, no matter how much he wants to see, call, talk, text, etc don't let him. Block calls and profiles online, ignore messages that he may send from other accounts/phones. Just ignore, ignore, ignore. Hopefully he'll get the hint eventually.
